nodes.label: Layerwise FFN Importance Analysis
nodes.author: Wataru Ikeda, Kazuki Yano, et al.
nodes.rationale: Investigation of position-dependent importance of feed-forward networks in Transformer LMs; demonstrates that concentrating FFNs in 70% of middle layers outperforms standard configurations.

nodes.label: FFN-Expanded Layer
nodes.rationale: Transformer layer with expanded intermediate representation dimension in FFN; used to concentrate FFN computational capacity in specific layers while maintaining total parameter count.

nodes.label: FFN-Deactivated Layer
nodes.rationale: Transformer layer with FFN completely removed, consisting only of self-attention mechanism; used to test whether FFN functionality can be redistributed to other layers.

nodes.label: Layer Placement Positions
nodes.rationale: Three positional configurations for FFN-expanded layers: first (near input), middle (center), and final (near output); enables investigation of position-dependent FFN importance.

nodes.label: Middle 70% Configuration
nodes.rationale: Optimal FFN configuration concentrating 70% of FFN parameters in consecutive middle layers; consistently outperforms baseline across model scales (285M-1.2B parameters).

nodes.label: FFN Knowledge Storage Hypothesis
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that FFNs primarily serve to store knowledge from training data, functioning similarly to key-value memory; motivates investigation of optimal FFN positioning.

nodes.label: LLaMA Transformer Architecture
nodes.rationale: De facto standard Transformer LM architecture with pre-LN, SwiGLU activation, and RoPE positional encoding; used as basis for FFN importance analysis.

nodes.label: FineWeb-Edu Pretraining Dataset
nodes.rationale: Dataset used for pretraining baseline and experimental models in FFN importance study.

nodes.label: Zero-Shot Relation Extraction (zsRE) Knowledge Assessment
nodes.rationale: Evaluation method using knowledge-based QA pairs to measure model's ability to retrieve factual information; assesses FFN knowledge storage capacity.

nodes.label: FFN Layer Placement and Scaling in Language Models
nodes.rationale: Investigates optimal placement of FFN-expanded layers across transformer depth to improve model performance under compute-optimal training, finding middle layers most important.

nodes.label: FFN Layer Importance Across Depth
nodes.rationale: Finding that middle layers of transformers are most important for FFN expansion, with first and final layers showing negative or minimal importance.

nodes.label: Middle FFN Layers Most Important
nodes.rationale: Empirical finding that expanding FFN in middle 70% of layers yields best performance, with diminishing returns at extremes.

nodes.label: FFN Placement Ablation Study
nodes.rationale: Systematic evaluation of first/middle/final FFN placement at 10-90% ratios across 4 model sizes and 8 downstream tasks.
